title: Sampling policy translator and consistent trace markers for exporters
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Implement a sampling policy translator and a stable trace marker that we attach to spans so downstream backends (OTLP exporters, Jaeger HTTP/Thrift, Tempo ingest) can honor Redwood's sampling decisions and preserve consistent sampling metadata across traces, metrics, and logs. Motivation: downstream trace backends have differing conventions for sample flags, tag names, and retention semantics. Customers using Dedicated/Private deployments and Redwood routing expect consistent sampling across observability signals so debug sessions, quality metrics, and billing attribution line up. This ticket implements: 1) a translator service (library + small gateway hook) that maps Redwood sampling policy (rate, head-based, tail-based, debug retain) to exporter-specific attributes; 2) a canonical trace marker header/span-attribute (redwood.sample.v1) that carries sample decision, sample-rate, and policy-id; 3) logic to preserve parent-sampled semantics across service boundaries; 4) per-tenant override hooks and fail-open behavior when exporter compatibility is uncertain; 5) compatibility shims for Jaeger legacy flags and Tempo ingestion nuances (batch vs streaming). Deliverables: design doc with compatibility table, OTLP processor changes, exporter adapters for Jaeger/Tempo, e2e tests with synthetic traces, perf microbench to measure added cost, docs for customers and Console UI flag to surface sampling policy mapped to exporter capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Redwood produces redwood.sample.v1 on every sampled trace and downstream exporters receive an equivalent representation (Jaeger tag or Tempo attribute) for >99% of test traces; 2) Parent sampling propagation preserved across RPC boundaries in simulated 3-hop call graph; 3) Per-tenant override applied and verifiable via test harness; 4) No P95 latency increase >2ms for span ingestion in the fast-path; 5) E2E tests covering debug-retain traffic show retained traces in Jaeger/Tempo for debug TTL period; 6) Console shows mapping matrix in observability settings and an audit log entry when override is set.
tests: Unit tests for translator (policy -> exporter attributes); integration tests using local Jaeger/Tempo clusters (minikube CI job); synthetic workload that validates parent/child sampling propagation; perf microbench comparing baseline to feature on 1k RPS trace generator; mutation tests to ensure fallback behaviors; end-to-end sampling rate stability check over 24h simulation.
implementation_notes:
- Add an OTLP processing stage (processor name: sampling_translator) that inserts redwood.sample.v1 attribute and maps to exporter wire formats.
- Exporter adapters will translate redwood.sample.v1 into: Jaeger tag 'redwood.sample_v1' + j.sampling.priority where available; Tempo: attribute 'redwood.sample.v1' and ensure ingestion accepts attribute on HTTP/GRPC ingest.
- Per-tenant config lives in tenant-config store; default mapping table in code + runtime overrides from Console.
- For legacy Jaeger ingestion (Thrift over UDP) we fall back to injecting a dedicated binary tag and an inflight header for agents that support it.
- Add a small compatibility test harness in infra/observability/testbench that spins up each backend and validates attribute presence.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated by tenant flag (off by default) in test orgs. 2) Enable for internal staging tenants and run 48h soak with 10k traces/min. 3) Gradual ramp to customer tenants with per-tenant opt-in through Console. 4) Monitor ingestion error rates and trace loss; rollback toggle available. 5) Post-rollout: enable mapping visibility in Console and update onboarding docs.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: sampling-mismatch-rate, translator-latency, exporter-attr-drop-rate. Alerts: sampling-mismatch-rate > 0.5% for 10m (P0), translator-latency P95 > 5ms (P1), exporter-attr-drop-rate > 1% for 5m. Create one-time ad-hoc Grafana panel for rollout window to track retention of debug traces.
